requires: The immutable MH-C-BASELINE-001 artifact, accepted MH-ADR-0004 compatibility policy, legacy Python package, router, and discovery product entry point are present.

Every case has a unique stable ID, exactly one outcome category from success, refuted, unsupported, timeout, or error, a supported invocation surface, JSON-compatible arguments, and an explicit expected stable-field policy.
Capture runs against a clean committed source revision whose 40-character Git object identity and MathHead source-tree identity are recorded in the corpus provenance.

At least ten representative cases cover every required outcome category, both the routed result surface and discovery verdict surface, conclusive and inconclusive results, and stable witness or evidence fields where emitted.
ensures: Capture mode writes one canonical UTF-8 JSON corpus containing contract identity, exact source provenance, normalization policy, ordered case inputs, normalized expected outputs, and per-case stable-output SHA-256 identities.

Replay mode invokes every case through its declared legacy public entry point, applies only the corpus-declared normalization rules, and compares the complete normalized result with the committed expected output.

Success, refuted, unsupported, timeout, and error remain distinct outcome categories; replay never converts an inconclusive or rejected result into success and never weakens a stable verdict, reason code, witness, evidence tier, or explanation.

Only meta.elapsed_ms and backend version metadata at meta.sympy_version or meta.z3_version may be normalized; each normalized field must exist with its declared JSON type and is replaced by a path-specific typed sentinel rather than deleted.
Case order is ascending by stable ID, mapping keys are canonical, sets and tuples become JSON arrays in deterministic order, and every stable output identity is computed after normalization.

Check mode is read-only, fails on stale corpus bytes or provenance, and distinguishes malformed corpus, invocation failure, per-case timeout, semantic drift, and unsupported host profile with nonzero exit results.
A mutation to a case input, category, surface, expected stable field, output identity, source provenance, or normalization allowlist is rejected by an independent validator.
The compatibility corpus is a differential migration oracle, not a new promise for incidental legacy internals; known incorrect trust claims must still be corrected under MH-ADR-0004.
raises: No Python exception crosses the command boundary for malformed JSON, unknown fields, duplicate IDs, unsupported surfaces, missing entry points, non-JSON results, invocation failure, timeout, stale output, or semantic drift.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit from in-process library execution are not reclassified as ordinary legacy results.
Programmer defects may produce a traceback only in explicit debug mode.

effects.filesystem: check mode is read-only except interpreter and test caches; capture mode may atomically replace only docs/reconstruction/legacy-compat-v1.json
effects.process: case execution occurs in bounded child processes so a product timeout cannot hang capture or replay; children are terminated, killed if necessary, waited, and reaped
effects.network: none after the selected MH-C-ENV-002 profile is bootstrapped
effects.repository: never edits PLAN, TODO, PROGRESS, accepted contracts, the immutable legacy baseline, observations, ADRs, source modules, or files outside the declared corpus output
effects.mutation: case arguments are decoded afresh for each invocation and no result may mutate committed corpus data

determinism.serialization: canonical JSON uses UTF-8, sorted mapping keys, stable separators, a trailing newline, and no clock, checkout path, runner identity, random value, or raw elapsed timing
determinism.case_order: cases are sorted lexicographically by stable ID and duplicate IDs fail closed
determinism.normalization: the exact allowlist is meta.elapsed_ms, meta.sympy_version, and meta.z3_version; typed sentinels preserve field presence and reject type drift
determinism.timeout: the timeout representative uses a fixed solver seed, accepted finite solver budget, bounded input, and a larger process watchdog; any non-timeout verdict is semantic drift
determinism.provenance: the corpus binds the source commit, MathHead source-tree SHA-256, accepted contract hash, and each normalized case-output SHA-256

budget.cancellation: terminate then kill the active child, wait for reaping, report the case ID, and return a distinct nonzero result

epistemics.current: all cases reproduced the complete normalized legacy outputs and all provenance and output identities matched
epistemics.drifted: a stable output, case input, category, identity, normalization rule, or source binding differs
epistemics.invalid: the corpus or contract is malformed, incomplete, ambiguous, unbound, or contains a non-allowlisted normalization
epistemics.timed_out: a child exceeded the corpus process watchdog; this is a replay failure distinct from the expected solver-timeout result category
epistemics.not_run: the corpus was inspected without executing every case; never equivalent to current

invariants: Every required outcome category has at least one representative and the complete corpus has at least ten cases.
Expected product timeout is represented inside a completed result envelope; a harness watchdog timeout is always a failed replay.
Stable result fields are compared recursively and byte-for-byte after canonical JSON serialization.
Normalization never removes a field, masks verdict or evidence semantics, accepts an arbitrary path, or rewrites case inputs.
Each committed case output identity equals the SHA-256 of its canonical normalized expected output.
The source tree used for capture contains no implementation changes from the MH-016 green legacy architecture.
Accepted contracts, ADRs, legacy baseline evidence, and observations remain byte-identical.
